summary: Justin Ritzinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and has served as a professor at Oberlin College.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where he was supervised by Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1797 to 1801. He subsequently held a position at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. After studies at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, he served as a professor at Kiel and later as Chief Librarian and Professor of Oriental Languages at Königsberg.
Jyotirindranath Tagore was active in Indology and other fields. He received his education at the Hindu School and Presidency University around 1864–1865.

János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University. He later worked as a research associate and lecturer at the University of Vienna and as a Buddhist studies researcher at IKGA.

Jérôme Ducor is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Jacques May. Attested in 2006, he served at the University of Lausanne in the Department of Oriental Languages and Cultures.

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski was a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at Vilnius and Kazan, he became a professor and rector at Kazan Federal University before holding a professorship at the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (circa 1914–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (circa 1920–1939), and he taught Constantin Regamey.

József Budenz was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, the latter under Theodor Benfey. He worked at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and served as full professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University.

Jörg Heimbel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and David P. Jackson. He has held appointments at Hamburg, Munich, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has served as a professor at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum.

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and later served there as an associate professor from circa 2006 to 2023.

Jürgen Hanneder specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Munich, Bonn, and Marburg, earning his PhD under Michael Hahn, and held posts at Bonn and Halle before becoming a professor at Marburg in 2007.

Jürgen Renn is a historian of science who completed his PhD at TU Berlin. He has served as a director at the Max Planck Institutes for the History of Science and Geoanthropology, alongside professorial posts at Boston University and Berlin.

Jōryū Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied and taught extensively at Ryukoku University, later serving as emeritus professor. He also directed the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute and the Shinshu Otaniha Institute.

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He held academic posts at Annamalai University and the University of Mysore.
K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indology scholar who served as a professor at the University of Lucknow and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer was an Indologist who served as secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945) and as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research.

K. Jayakumar is associated with Indology and linguistics. He was educated at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School in Thiruvananthapuram and served in the Indian Administrative Service from circa 1978 to 2012.
